1.1.title: Structure of Water and Hydrogen Bonding
1.1.how_points_are_earned: You earn points by connecting a property of water to the molecular reason behind it and then to the biological consequence.
1.1.answer_move: Use a three-step chain: water is polar -> hydrogen bonds form -> this causes the biological property or effect.
1.1.common_point_loss: Naming a water property without explaining how polarity or hydrogen bonding produces it.

2.5.title: Membrane Transport
2.5.how_points_are_earned: You earn points by identifying the gradient, direction of movement, energy requirement, and protein involvement.
2.5.answer_move: State high-to-low or low-to-high relative to the gradient, then name passive or active transport.
2.5.common_point_loss: Ignoring gradient direction or claiming all protein transport requires ATP.

3.1.title: Enzymes
3.1.how_points_are_earned: You earn points by connecting active-site shape, substrate specificity, and activation energy to reaction outcomes.
3.1.answer_move: Describe how enzyme structure affects substrate binding and reaction rate.
3.1.common_point_loss: Saying enzymes add energy to reactions instead of lowering activation energy.

5.3.title: Mendelian Genetics
5.3.how_points_are_earned: You earn points by assigning genotypes, setting up crosses, and interpreting probabilities or phenotypic ratios.
5.3.answer_move: Define alleles and parental genotypes before building the Punnett square or probability setup.
5.3.common_point_loss: Reporting ratios without connecting them to genotype and allele segregation.

7.5.title: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium
7.5.how_points_are_earned: You earn points by using p + q = 1 and p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 and interpreting departures from expected frequencies.
7.5.answer_move: Identify p and q carefully, calculate genotype frequencies, then compare observed and expected values.
7.5.common_point_loss: Taking the square root of the wrong frequency or forgetting that 2pq is the heterozygote frequency.
